newsitem.title: USA: HFS says Interval sale effort progressing.
newsitem.headline: HFS says Interval sale effort progressing.

text.p: Travel and real estate giant HFS said Tuesday its effort to divest the vacation timeshare business of merger partner CUC International Inc. is progressing and is not expecting any significant delays.
Goldman Sachs has been retained to sell the Interval International business, HFS Chairman Henry Silverman said in a telephone interview.

"The books are out and we expect probably about 30 bidders, plus or minus, and I hope that it can be accomplished on a timely basis to fit within the parameters of our planned merger timetable," Silverman said.
U.S. antitrust regulators had issued a second request for the proposed $11 billion transaction due to concerns about potential overlap in the companies' vacation timeshare exchange businesses.

The companies previously had targeted completion of the deal by the end of the third quarter and "that is still a reasonable expectation, plus or minus a few weeks," Silverman said. HFS franchises include real estate firm Century 21 and lodging brands Ramada and Howard Johnson.
